verdict: PARTIALLY REFUTED. Five things check out against the sources: the equations, the mode table rows, the SAFETY-1 diagnosis, the pinouts, and the 11 to 5 package count. Pinouts were checked against the SN74LVC3G04 DCT, 2G08/2G32 DCT and 1G11 DCK pin tables, and they match D:1880-1885. Counted against B.3 (D:1675-1693), r8 had 11 LVC packages and the reduction leaves 5 (U105, U106, U107, U110, U118). However, the analysis is wrong or incomplete in seven places. (1) The proposed SAFETY-2 fix opens the R3 loop on purpose. (2) A single short in the tap harness defeats the SAFETY-1 fix. (3) A stuck-HIGH QUAL is now an unbounded latent fault. (4) A hang during qualification is not bounded, because R5 is only required for FC windows. (5) The blank-loss item ignores the FC clamp that RFC_OFF puts back. (6) The new slow-edge input on QUAL is not listed. (7) Calling the CR 3V3 loss 'undetected' overstates it. The outcome claim "R3' holds in every mode, provided I-9 and R5" holds only as a register-backed claim. It does not hold as a hardware-backed claim against single faults on T5/T6/T10.
errors: SAFETY-2 fix creates the hazard it is meant to detect. The fix runs in Run-entry qualification: REGEN is HIGH, MOT_PWR is HIGH, BT is on the bus, and REL is 1 through the QUAL term. If /CE is stuck LOW, writing EN_CHG = 1 starts bus -> charger -> pack -> BT boost -> bus charging. That is the R3' loop (D:58). The 5 ms pass window is also shorter than the BQ25798 charge-start and CHG_STAT update latency, TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C REG1C / charge-enable deglitch), so a stuck /CE LOW can pass the test. If the check is kept, it should run only with BT_BUS LOW (FC-only selection), or VINDPM should be set >= 18.2 V and the BQ25798 input current, not IBAT, should be observed. Better, the operator should be asked to accept SAFETY-2 as latent with a T-C-05 build check.

Blank-loss item (section 1.1) is internally inconsistent. After H1 falls inside a window, the analysis's own RFC_OFF = FCCN + H1*UVB drops to 0. Q202 then turns on, and the FC clamp of 0.65-0.95 A on the ILIM pin (D:1854-1856) bounds the draw in hardware, whatever IINDPM 1.70 A says (EN_EXTILIM = 1, D:2913). The draw is therefore not held only by VINDPM and OC_FC. The exception is if the ILIM pin is latched only at POR (D:230 says 'the pin is read at POR'). Whether the pin is re-read continuously (T-B-07) decides which statement is true, so the row needs that dependency stated, not the current claim.

Hang in qualification: the analysis says 'the watchdog reset drops QUAL through R123'. But G.3 (D:3017-3030) makes R5 a precondition for FC windows only, and the B-table row at D:257 calls it 'future watchdog only'. With R5 unfitted, an MCU hang with QUAL HIGH, REGEN HIGH and MOT_PWR HIGH keeps the converter released from the bus indefinitely. r8 bounded this with tw_QQ 0.20-0.46 s and ARM_OK (D:229, D:1504). The bound is now none. Either R5 + T-W-01 becomes a precondition for any Run entry, not only FC windows, or this is listed as a new accepted cost. TR section 6 item 6 covers a firmware slip, not a hang without a watchdog.

'CR 3V3 lost: Undetected' is overstated. With P5 HIGH and the converter held off, a brake (H1 readback on pin 34 reads LOW while V_rgn > V_bus) gives zero CHG_IIN on pin 22 (T17, which is kept) and no I2C IBUS/charge status. That is a plausibility signature firmware can trip on. It is not undetectable, only no longer hardware-sensed.

Section 1 row 'Run cruise, regen armed: hard converter-off' and T-D-02(b)/(c) (D:3261): the T-D-02 pass criterion '/CE > 1.3 V and IBAT < 10 mA within TW_HB_MAX' for a hang in regen-armed cruise or mid-burst can no longer be met, because ARM_OK is gone. The analysis does not flag that T-D-02 must be rewritten, (b)/(c) retired or re-specified.
missed_cases: Common-cause harness short T5-T6, which defeats the SAFETY-1 fix and the r8 barrier. T6 carries unprotected MB 3V3: R175 68 ohm sits at F07 on the CR end (D:672). T5 is the bare D-BC-FC EN net (J1.45), and R122 is CR-side (D:669, D:1915). A wire, insulation or adjacent-cavity short on the new single tap connector (lead decision) pulls the EN net toward 3V3 against Teensy pin 31. If the net exceeds VEN_R max 1.4 V, FC_CHARGE is truly ON with BT_BUS HIGH. U119 and U120 both see a real HIGH, so FCC_ON*NOT FCC_OFF = 1, REL = 1 and /CE is LOW in regen-armed cruise. This is the SAFETY-1 condition, held only by the VINDPM 18.62-19.38 V register, and the switch is also physically closed. r8 blocked it with BTB_OFF*BT_OK in H2c (D:1526). Whether the Teensy pad or the 3V3 rail wins is TODO(verify: i.MX RT1062 pad drive vs 3V3 source impedance). Mitigations: a pin-order rule that keeps T6 non-adjacent to T5 and T10 with GND guards, and/or a firmware trip on V_chg (pin 38) rising or CHG_IIN > 0 while FCC is commanded LOW.

QUAL stuck HIGH (pin 10 stuck, or the T10 tap shorted to T6/3V3) is now an unbounded latent single fault. D:2496 relied on the U111 tw_QQ bound and on FR-08(a) on pin 33, and both are removed. When P5 is LOW with FCC LOW (T6/T7 tails, T9 re-qualify, the FR-47(a) pack-OV P5 drop, any trip in regen-armed Run), REL = 1 indefinitely and the bus powers the BQ25798 SYS path with /CE HIGH. T-D-13 (D:3272) loses its pass criterion. Combined with SAFETY-2 (/CE stuck LOW, also latent), this gives the full R3' loop from two dormant faults with no detection between them. The analysis lists SAFETY-1 and SAFETY-2 but not this third latent fault, nor the latent-fault accumulation.

QUAL now feeds a plain SN74LVC1G11 input (U107). It used to feed the Schmitt B input of U111 (D:1693). On a Teensy reset or high-Z, QUAL falls through R123 47 kOhm with a slow edge. The D:1691 exception list (CHG_ARM, FCCEIL) and the T-D-01 test must add QUAL. Also, pin 5 now carries R130 + EIB R267 47k, while QUAL has only R123 47k. The two nets fall at different rates, so QUAL can stay above VIH after P5N has gone HIGH. This is harmless only if QUAL was LOW before the reset. That premise should be stated.

Ordering requirement not stated: firmware must drop QUAL (pin 10) before it raises P5 (pin 5) at the end of qualification. /CE now follows pin 5 through R130 and U201 only. The NOT P5 mask travels through U105 -> U107 -> U110 -> ribbon -> U201 -> the Q203/Q201 gates, which are 47 kOhm-pulled and switch on a microsecond scale. If P5 rises first, /CE goes LOW while ILIM is still released and the bus feeds the charger. This window is microseconds long and probably harmless given the charge-start latency, TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C /CE response), but it is a new transition in the F.5 T1 step list.

T5 tap open, or R122 open, not enumerated. Checked: R187 3.30 MOhm against the U120 1.45 MOhm divider gives about 1.0 V at the tap. FCC_OFF then reads LOW and FCC_ON reads LOW, so FCCN = 0 and FCCP = 0. Qualification can never release, and FC windows cannot release (RFC_OFF = H1*UVB). This fails safe and announces itself at Run entry. Add it to the table for completeness.

The SAFETY-1 robustness argument holds for an internal stuck-at of U119: U119 stuck LOW blocks QF and is detected at Run entry, and U119 stuck HIGH makes FCCP = 0 and disables FC windows. It does not hold for any fault that drives the shared T5 node itself. That is the harness short above, or a stuck-HIGH Teensy pin 31 / D-BC-FC EN net. In those cases both comparators agree on a real HIGH, and no hardware loop barrier remains.
